transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I spend so much time trying to fix how I look before I go out that I end up missing things with my family and at work. It's really starting to take over my life, and my doctor recommended I come get an evaluation.

When you are getting ready, are you mainly worried that there is something wrong or ugly about your appearance that others will notice, or do you also have repeated unwanted thoughts and rituals about other things like contamination, checking, or symmetry?

No, it's really just about my appearance—specifically, I'm constantly worried that my face looks crooked, saggy, and lopsided. I'll spend hours checking mirrors, changing clothes, and asking people if I look weird, but I don't have any of those other fears like contamination or symmetry.
Do you ever feel that the appearance problem is actually much smaller than it seems, or that other people would say you look normal, but you still can’t stop worrying about it?

People constantly tell me that I look completely fine or normal for my age, but I just can't stop worrying about it. When I look in the mirror, all I can see is a saggy, lopsided, and unattractive face, so their reassurance doesn't really help me. I just get completely stuck obsessing over it and trying to fix it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with hypochondriacal disorder / body dysmorphic-type preoccupation coded here as F45.2: the patient has a persistent preoccupation with perceived facial defects that others consider minimal or absent, spends excessive time checking mirrors and seeking reassurance, and experiences clear life interference. OCD is less likely because the thoughts and rituals are narrowly focused on appearance rather than multiple intrusive obsessions/compulsions.
